cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Financial Analyst role at Jamf. The posting describes financial decision support for leadership: KPI analysis, forecasting, budgeting and support for the monthly close. That is the core of my current job, and I am ready to do it at a larger scale.

For the past three years I have been the Financial Manager at AMG Family Dental in Belmont, MA. I build the annual operating budget and the monthly forecasts, run budget-vs-actual variance analysis, and put together KPI reports for ownership. I also found and recovered more than $500K in annual revenue by tightening our financial reporting and reconciliation in Dentrix, and I cut A/R aging by 10% by streamlining insurance claim submission and follow-up.

You ask analysts to look for ways to use AI and automation. I have done this in practice. I wrote a Python process that automated our weekly insurance payment reconciliation, cutting the work from 5 hours to 1 and flagging underpaid claims for follow-up. My skills also include advanced Excel, SQL, Tableau and Python, which I would use to build the reports and metrics the role calls for.

Earlier, as a Financial Analyst Intern at Northrop Grumman, I audited more than 100 financial models for accuracy and internal controls, and I analyzed supplier costs and budget variances across multiple programs, then presented recommendations to senior leadership. I hold an M.A. in International Economics and Finance from Brandeis and a B.S. in Finance from Suffolk.

I am a U.S. citizen, available immediately, and comfortable working remotely. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support Jamf's finance team.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian

Dear Hiring Manager,

What I do have is a record of persistent follow-up, comfort talking about money, and the ability to explain a recommendation to senior people.

That work taught me to stay organized across many open items and to keep following up politely until something is resolved, which is the habit your SDR role depends on.

Your buyers will be weighing the cost of a security tool against risk and budget. I have spent three years building budgets, forecasts and variance reports, so I am comfortable speaking that language. At Northrop Grumman I presented cost-saving recommendations to senior leadership, and at FYND in Tokyo I presented AI adoption recommendations to the co-founders. Outside work, I was on the Brandeis intramural basketball team that won the 2023 championship and I serve on the executive board of the Armenian Church Youth Organization of America at St. James Church. I like being part of a competitive team and being accountable to it. I am available immediately and can commute to Burlington.

Thank you for your time. I would be glad to talk about how I can contribute to Black Duck's pipeline.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian
